subject: Intermittent large-payload failures — dual-homed private gateway routing + MTU
messages:
From: Sara Davis <sara.davis@deltacorp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: networkops@deltacorp.com
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: intermittent large-inference failures over private link

Hi Alex / Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent failures for large inference requests from our private deployment that started after the weekend cutover to the dual-homed gateway. Symptoms: requests with long prompts (~>12k tokens) sometimes fail mid-token with TCP retransmits and "connection reset by peer". Smaller requests succeed. Attaching a short tcpdump and a raw route extract.

What we've observed:
- Client -> Redwood model endpoint over private VPC tunnel (Delta colo)
- Failures correlate with packets ~1500-1600 bytes (segmented) and a string of retransmits
- tcpdump shows DF=1 on some packets and ICMP "fragmentation needed" isn't getting back consistently
- Route flaps seen in the colo BGP neighbors around the same times (we're including the ibgp dump)

Attachments: tcpdump-20260509.pcap.gz, ibgp-routes-raw.txt

Can you help triage? We opened INC-7842 with our on-call.

Thanks,
Sara Davis
Network Engineer, DeltaCorp
Network Operations

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Davis <sara.davis@deltacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent large-inference failures over private link

Sara — thanks for the quick report and attachments. I've looped in Laura (network infra) and Dev (runtime) to help investigate. Initial hypothesis: a combination of MTU overhead from our VXLAN/private tunnel + asymmetric routing from the dual-homed gateway causing PMTU discovery to fail. That could explain why larger requests fail intermittently while smaller ones succeed.

Next steps from our side (we'll take these in parallel):
1) Laura: can you sanity-check the ibgp dump and confirm whether both colo paths are active and if there's any route-target / import-export mismatch that could cause asymmetric return paths?
2) Dev: please review tcpdump for signs of GSO/GRO offload and if the runtime is seeing RSTs or retransmit-induced connection ulcers.
3) Sara / Delta: please, if possible, temporarily allow ICMP-type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) across the path so PMTU can converge — we realize this may be a policy ask.

We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth. If we find a short mitigation (MSS clamp, temporary MSS adjust, or a one-off route pin), we'll propose it.

Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Sara Davis <sara.davis@deltacorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent large-inference failures over private link

Thanks Alex — I pulled the ibgp dump and the topo from our colo partner. Quick notes:
- Both uplinks are flapping between the two provider-facing VRFs; we see routes for the Delta /26 being installed via VRF-A and VRF-B at different times.
- There is an oddity: the route-target import/export on VRF-B was not advertising the customer's RT correctly after the cutover; that can lead to inbound traffic taking a different path back to Delta.
- The colo edge firewall is performing SNAT for egress traffic (policy-based SNAT). Combined with our gateway doing a second SNAT for legacy reasons, you can get asymmetric flow where return traffic is not matching the original flow state.

On the MTU side:
- Our VXLAN overlay adds ~50 bytes of overhead; their tunnel MTU is 1500, so some packets are hitting >1450 effective payload and require fragmentation.
- With DF set and ICMP3/4 blocked on parts of the path, PMTU cannot converge and you see the behavior you described.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk):
- Ask Delta NetOps to temporarily allow ICMP type 3/code 4 across both paths so PMTU discovery can work.
- Apply an MSS clamp of 1400 on the colo gateway (we can roll this ourselves if you prefer) to avoid fragmented packets.
- Verify and correct RT import/export on VRF-B so both paths advertise/accept the same RTs.

I'll attach a short test plan for MSS clamp and a sample iptables/sysctl snippet. Dev — please check if the runtime logs show RSTs or retransmit timeouts on the model worker side; that will help confirm whether packets are dropped mid-stream.

--
Laura Bennett
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Sara Davis <sara.davis@deltacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent large-payload failures over private link

Quick runtime findings after looking at the pcap and worker logs:
- We see a pattern of repeated DUP ACKs and one-side RSTs when the client-side segmented packets exceed ~1448 payload.
- The model process does not explicitly close the connection; the RST looks network-originated.
- GSO/GRO artifacts are present in the pcap. On our side workers, tcpdump on host shows aggregated segments; however the kernel is handing the segments to the containerized process fine unless the packet actually gets fragmented on the wire.

Planned short test (I attached mss-clamp-test-plan.md):
1) Apply iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu on the colo gateway for Delta IPs (quick test window). Example: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -o vxlan0 -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
2) If iptables not available on the device, set sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on a test host and monitor (less ideal long-term).
3) Keep ICMP open during the test and capture another pcap for comparison.

I'll be on the test window tomorrow 05/11 08:30 - 09:30 PT if Delta can open a short maintenance window.

- Dev

Subject: Re: Production: intermittent large-payload failures over private link

Thanks everyone — quick summary and agreed next steps: 

Summary:
- Root causes likely a combination of (a) VRF import/export mismatch causing asymmetric return paths, (b) double SNAT at colo + gateway, and (c) PMTU blackhole due to VXLAN overhead and ICMP filtered on some hops.

Immediate actions (today / 24hr):
1) Delta NetOps (Sara): please enable ICMP type3/code4 across the two colo paths for the test window and confirm the maintenance window for tomorrow 08:30 PT.
2) Laura / Redwood network: we'll correct the RT import/export on VRF-B and temporarily disable the redundant SNAT on our gateway for the Delta prefix (will coordinate with colo).
3) Dev: execute the MSS clamp test in the maintenance window and capture pcap. If MSS clamp reduces the failure rate, we'll propose a permanent clamp on the gateway.
4) Marissa: I'm keeping you in the loop for any commercial fallout (Tier-1 customers impacted).

If we don't see improvement after the clamp + RT fix, we'll escalate to the colo on-call for a forced pin of the return path and consider routing all Delta traffic via a single stable path until a config fix is completed.

I'll post results in this thread after the test.
